_comment: The Competitive Intelligence agent's watchlist. PUT this to /api/intel/watchlist.
Every URL here was fetched on 2026-08-24 with the agent's own User-Agent and run
through its own extractText(), so each one is known to return usable prose rather
than a JavaScript shell or a bot block. Re-verify before adding anything: a source
that 403s is worse than no source, because it reports 'unreachable' every week
forever and trains you to ignore the column.
Three candidates were rejected for exactly that reason and are listed at the bottom.
On 'kind': almost nothing here is a competitor, and that is the point. Velvex returns
a structural reading; these return a number. You do not watch a company because it
matches you today, you watch it because it is where a match would first appear, and
the language always moves before the product does.

sources.label: Lumena Global — Operational Readiness Assessment
sources.note: The closest adjacent ground found, and the only one using the same rhetorical move: 'Strategy tells you where to go. An operational readiness assessment tells you whether the current version of your business can get there.' Not the same product: their seven pillars are operating-model and org design (decision rights, role clarity, cadence, handoffs), the engagement runs 2 to 4 weeks, and no price is published. Watch three things. Whether their pillars move from process toward commercial architecture, revenue mechanics, channel dependency or margin. Whether a fixed price appears. Whether the 2 to 4 week window shortens.

sources.label: Startup Readiness Score — startupready.ai
sources.note: Free six-pillar startup assessment. Structurally the nearest analogue to the Vela node framing, at the opposite end of depth and price. Watch whether the pillars acquire dependency language, whether a paid tier appears, and whether they start claiming the output is defensible rather than indicative.

sources.label: BizHealth.ai — homepage
sources.note: AI business health diagnostic across financial, operational, team and strategic health. Watch for the word 'architecture', for anything about load-bearing dependencies, and for whether they move from benchmarking against peers to reading one business on its own terms. Benchmarking and structural reading are different claims.

sources.label: BizHealth.ai — best business diagnostic tools index
sources.note: A category-defining index page: it decides who counts as a business diagnostic tool and in what words. This is where category language hardens, and it is the single most useful page on this list for tracking how 'business health' is being defined by the people selling it. Velvex appearing on a page like this, or the criteria shifting toward structural reading, are both events.

sources.label: ReadyScore.ai — investor readiness score
sources.note: Scores investor readiness across 40+ parameters. Already repositioning: as of 2026-08-24 this domain redirects to investorconnect365.com, so the standalone scoring product is being folded into a marketplace. Watch whether the score survives as its own product or becomes a funnel into introductions, which is a different business from a diagnostic.

sources.label: ScrollLaunch — Startup Readiness Assessment
sources.note: Free six-pillar diagnostic. Watch the pillar names and whether 'diagnostic' starts being used for something structural rather than for a questionnaire. The word is being taken, and this is one of the places it is being taken from.

sources.label: Avantiico — fixed-price readiness assessment
sources.note: Not a competitor by subject, but the closest published analogue to Velvex's commercial model: a bounded, fixed-price diagnostic delivered in days rather than an open-ended engagement, sold explicitly against 'eight-week multi-stream consulting'. Watch how they justify the fixed price and how they describe the boundary of the engagement. That argument is the same argument Velvex has to make.

sources.label: Finro — startup due diligence and fundraising readiness
sources.note: How founders are taught to prepare for diligence. This is the vocabulary a buyer arrives with, which matters more than what any competitor says: it determines whether 'structural dependency' lands as precise or as jargon.

sources.label: Neotas — investment due diligence checklist
sources.note: The allocator side of the same conversation, and it already uses 'structural' and 'dependency'. Watch whether operational and commercial architecture rise up the checklist relative to financial diligence. If they do, the pre-raise position Velvex would occupy is being validated by the buyers themselves.

sources.label: Magistral — commercial due diligence for buyers
sources.note: Commercial diligence framed for acquirers. Notably free of structural vocabulary today, which makes it a clean control: if this page starts talking about dependencies and load-bearing channels, the language has moved in the part of the market that writes cheques.

_rejected.why: SCOREMAX. Returns 403 to our User-Agent, so it cannot be snapshotted or diffed. Worth a manual look now and then instead: it is an AI startup evaluation platform and a real category member, it just cannot be watched automatically.
Hello Alice Business Health Score. Returns 429. Relevant, since 'Business Health Score' is one of the exact terms being tracked, but rate limited against us.
